subject: Clarify package boundaries, token rounding, and sample invoice
messages:
From: Ethan Miller <ethan@brightcart.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Question on billing: token rounding & package boundaries

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers look promising. Before we move to an internal finance review, a few questions came up about how Redwood will meter and invoice our usage. Could you confirm the following?

1) Token rounding rules: if we send a 43-token prompt and get a 157-token response, does Redwood round per-message to the nearest 10 tokens, or is there per-session aggregation? Any minimum per-request charge?

2) Context/package boundaries: our app will mix short chat messages (mostly <=256 tokens) and occasional long batch summarizations (up to 12k). Will the long calls be billed differently (separate SKU or the same token unit)? Any automatic truncation or implicit splitting we should be aware of?

3) Discounts & packaging: we have a committed monthly SOW model in mind — is there a recommended packaging (seat + token commit vs. flat context-limited SKU) that tends to reduce unit costs for mixed workloads?

If you can send a short example invoice showing the rounding/aggregation and a proposed packaging to reduce churn, that would help our procurement team.

Best,
Ethan
Ethan Miller
Lead Platform Engineer, BrightCart

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Miller <ethan@brightcart.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-13T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on billing: token rounding & package boundaries

Hi Ethan — great question and thanks for laying this out clearly. Quick answers up front, then a short example invoice attached. Looping in Kim (billing) and Karthik (packaging/contract) to confirm the math and packaging recommendations.

Summary answer:
- Rounding: We do per-request rounding at the invoice line level using a configurable quantum. For BrightCart pilot we can set a 10-token quantum; default is 1 token. Rounding only affects the line item math, not model quality or internal throttling.
- Aggregation: We can optionally aggregate across a logical session (conversation_id) for committed SKUs to reduce rounding noise — that's a contract-level opt-in.
- Long context calls: Calls that exceed the 16k model context are automatically rejected; calls >8k are billed using the same per-token meter but we offer a separate long-context SKU with a lower per-token rate for committed volumes.
- Packaging: For mixed workloads we typically recommend a blended commit (monthly token reserve at a discounted rate) + overage per-token. For Stepped discounts we can also offer a small seat component for admin features.

Attached: BrightCart_Proposal_v2.pdf (sample pricing & sample invoice) and a quick sample-invoice spreadsheet.

Action items:
- @Kimberly: can you confirm the 10-token quantum for pilot pricing and the sample invoice numbers?
- @Karthik: please propose 2 packaging options (pure commit vs blended commit+seat) with unit economics for the volumes Ethan mentioned.

Ethan — I added short bullets above; see the attached example invoice. If you'd like, we can provision a short pilot commit so your procurement has real numbers to sign off.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-05-14T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on billing: token rounding & package boundaries

Ethan — quick follow-up with concrete math (see inline). I've pulled the sample invoice into the spreadsheet we attached; pasted below are the simplified line items so it's easy to reason about rounding impact.

Example scenario (one long summarization + three short chats in a day):
- Summarization call: prompt 1,240 tokens + response 3,980 tokens = 5,220 tokens. With 10-token quantum rounding -> billed tokens = ceil(5220 / 10) * 10 = 5,220 (already a multiple of 10)
- Chat A: prompt 38 + response 92 = 130 -> billed = ceil(130/10)*10 = 130
- Chat B: prompt 21 + response 57 = 78 -> billed = ceil(78/10)*10 = 80 (2-token overhead due to quantum)
- Chat C: prompt 12 + response 15 = 27 -> billed = ceil(27/10)*10 = 30 (3-token overhead)

Total raw tokens = 5,455. Total billed with 10-token quantum if not aggregated across session = 5,520 -> effective rounding overhead = 65 tokens (~1.2%).

If we enable session-level aggregation for the three small chats (they share a conversation_id), their combined raw = 235 -> billed = 240 (1 overhead) so total billed becomes 5,480 -> overhead ~25 tokens (0.46%).

Packaging recommendation (two options):
1) Pilot blended commit: 5M tokens/month reserved at $0.0008/token + overage at $0.0012/token; includes session-aggregation enabled and 10-token quantum by default for pilot.
2) Seat+Commit: $2,500/month seat for admin/tooling + 3M token commit at $0.0009/token + overage $0.0011/token; long-context SKU (calls >8k) discounted further by 15% if >= 250k long-context tokens/month.

I've added the sample-invoice lines: invoice shows per-line raw tokens, quantum, billed tokens, unit price, and line total. File: sample-invoice-ACCT-BR3921.xlsx.

Let me know if you want me to draft language for the SOW that explicitly states "session-aggregation opt-in" and the quantum set for the pilot.

Thanks,
Kim
Director, Billing Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Ethan Miller <ethan@brightcart.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on billing: token rounding & package boundaries

Monica / Kim — this is super helpful, thanks. The example math makes the overhead tolerable; procurement will prefer the pilot blended commit (option 1) so they can see monthly variance before we commit seats. Two small asks before I send to legal:

1) Can you add a short note in the proposal that confirms "session-aggregation is available as an opt-in for committed SKUs and will be reflected as a single billed line per conversation_id for the invoice period"?
2) For transparency, can you include a short appendix describing how system rejects (exceeding context) are surfaced in the invoice (we prefer clear error codes so our SREs can map failures to billing).

If you can send a one-paragraph addendum and an updated sample-invoice (with the opt-in toggled on), we'll kick it over to procurement.

Best,
Ethan
Lead Platform Engineer, BrightCart
